name: Private rental MEES upgrade planner
demand: England had 4.9 million privately rented dwellings in 2024. Government estimates the policy could result in 1.75 million homes receiving upgrades by 2030, but that is an upgrade estimate, not a count of likely software buyers: https://www.gov.uk/government/statistics/dwelling-stock-estimates-in-england-2024/dwelling-stock-estimates-england-31-march-2024 and https://www.gov.uk/government/consultations/improving-the-energy-performance-of-privately-rented-homes-2025-update/outcome/improving-the-energy-performance-of-privately-rented-homes-government-response-html. The 2024 English Private Landlord Survey reported about 513,000 direct landlords in its deposit-scheme sample; 17% had five or more properties, representing 49% of tenancies. The survey says 47% had at least one property rated D or below, but its sample does not fully represent landlords whose agents register deposits, and its findings predate the 2026 policy decision: https://www.gov.uk/government/statistics/english-private-landlord-survey-2024-main-report/english-private-landlord-survey-2024-main-report. The 2024 English Housing Survey found 48% of private rented dwellings at EPC C and 37% at D; these are legacy EER figures, not a count of homes failing the new dual-metric standard: https://www.gov.uk/government/statistics/chapters-for-english-housing-survey-2024-to-2025-headline-findings-on-housing-quality-and-energy-efficiency/chapter-2-energy-efficiency. Search volume, app installs, product users and willingness to pay: unverified.
prices: A direct competitor advertises a free EPC planner and a £14.99 full plan, with additional properties at £9.99 each: https://landlordepcs.co.uk/. PropReady advertises £12.99, £19.99 and £29.99 monthly plans with an EPC upgrade planner: https://propready.co.uk/. Lettable lists £19, £49 and £99 monthly; its £49 plan includes MEES strategy and EPC planning: https://www.lettable.co/. Duewise lists £9.99 monthly or £99 yearly for its standard plan: https://duewise.co.uk/. These are published asking prices, not evidence of completed sales.

revenue_proof.claim: No independently verifiable revenue, paid-customer count or completed sales evidence for a direct private-landlord MEES planner found in the reviewed sources. The closest direct site publishes prices and a free tier; those do not prove revenue.

copy_speed: The earlier kill-check's finding of no free planner is overturned by a current direct offer: LandlordEPCs advertises a free planner with multi-property comparison, simulated improvements, exemption checks and a PDF roadmap; PropReady also markets portfolio upgrade planning. Neither site's launch date or usage is verified: https://landlordepcs.co.uk/ and https://propready.co.uk/for-portfolio-landlords. Dated adjacent announcements since April: Stead says its closed beta began May 2026 and includes EPC lookup, not a confirmed costed MEES planner: https://stead.space/press. Letavo's builder described a May 2026 launch, while also describing the product as waitlisted ahead of its iOS launch; a completed public launch is therefore unverified: https://hailes.tech/work/letavo. Lettable markets MEES strategy and EPC planning and cites a Q1 2026 design partner, but gives no launch date: https://www.lettable.co/. Cotality describes an established portfolio retrofit product used by landlords of over two million homes, a vendor claim with no event date on the page; it is a serious adjacent incumbent, though small-landlord fit and pricing are unclear: https://www.cotality.com/uk/products/portfolio.
platform_risk: The 1 October 2030 compliance date, £10,000 cap and fabric-plus-either-heating-or-smart-readiness standard are government policy decisions; the response says further primary and secondary legislation is planned, aiming to take effect in 2027, subject to Parliamentary approval. Treat rule logic and marketing claims as versioned and provisional until legislation and technical details are settled: https://www.gov.uk/government/consultations/improving-the-energy-performance-of-privately-rented-homes-2025-update/outcome/improving-the-energy-performance-of-privately-rented-homes-government-response-html. The official EPC service offers England and Wales bulk data and an API, while Scotland has a separate service; public EPC data therefore helps competitors as much as this product, and country coverage must be handled explicitly: https://get-energy-performance-data.communities.gov.uk/. The Home Energy Model launch was delayed in the official February 2026 update; its EPC consultation closed in March, so verify the latest release and metric status before building forecasts against it: https://www.gov.uk/government/consultations/home-energy-model-replacement-for-the-standard-assessment-procedure-sap and https://www.gov.uk/government/consultations/home-energy-model-energy-performance-certificates. HEM libraries are open source for non-statutory uses, which also lowers imitation barriers: https://www.gov.uk/guidance/energy-calculation-as-a-service-ecaas-access-the-home-energy-model.
defensible_asset: No strong moat is established: EPC records and policy rules are public, and direct competitors already advertise free or low-cost planners: https://get-energy-performance-data.communities.gov.uk/ and https://landlordepcs.co.uk/. A possible future asset is a permissioned history linking property evidence, invoices and actual assessor-confirmed upgrade outcomes across successive rule versions; that asset does not yet exist. Evidence handling matters because government policy calls for pre- and post-upgrade EPCs and provides for registered exemptions: https://www.gov.uk/government/consultations/improving-the-energy-performance-of-privately-rented-homes-2025-update/outcome/improving-the-energy-performance-of-privately-rented-homes-government-response-html.
build_effort: A read-only England-and-Wales MVP could combine EPC lookup, portfolio records, spend and evidence tracking, exemption status and exports. That is a moderate product build; a trustworthy property-specific recommendation engine against the new metrics is materially harder and depends on stable HEM/EPC rules. No reliable build-duration estimate is verified. Keep recommendations advisory and visibly tied to the rule version until the methodology is settled: https://get-energy-performance-data.communities.gov.uk/, https://www.gov.uk/government/consultations/improving-the-energy-performance-of-privately-rented-homes-2025-update/outcome/improving-the-energy-performance-of-privately-rented-homes-government-response-html, and https://www.gov.uk/government/consultations/home-energy-model-replacement-for-the-standard-assessment-procedure-sap.
channel: Use brand-led SEO, a free searchable EPC checker, contextual search ads, opt-in content and permission-based referrals from assessors or landlord groups. Do not cold email, text, WhatsApp or DM individuals or sole traders: ICO guidance treats social DMs as electronic mail and sole traders as individual subscribers, generally requiring consent or a valid soft opt-in: https://ico.org.uk/for-organisations/direct-marketing-and-privacy-and-electronic-communications/business-to-business-marketing/.
owner_hours_per_week: Unverified; the <=5 hours/week constraint is not demonstrated without a live product and measured support load.
desk_test: Within one workday, make a privacy-safe sample portfolio report using public EPC data and the published policy rules; compare it directly with the free LandlordEPCs planner and retain only a clear portfolio-evidence or workflow gap. Offer a clearly labelled, refundable £14.99 reservation through a landlord community that permits promotion or an opt-in audience; that price matches the direct competitor's advertised full plan. Count only an actual reservation as demand evidence, not survey intent or clicks. No cold contact: https://landlordepcs.co.uk/ and https://get-energy-performance-data.communities.gov.uk/.
red_flags: The thin planner proposition now fails its differentiation check: a free direct planner is advertised, with a paid close substitute at £14.99, and a second vendor markets portfolio EPC planning: https://landlordepcs.co.uk/ and https://propready.co.uk/. The 2024 landlord survey found that 65% of landlords with a D-or-below property said they had no plans to improve some or all of them; this is a pre-policy survey result, not proof of current refusal to act: https://www.gov.uk/government/statistics/english-private-landlord-survey-2024-main-report/english-private-landlord-survey-2024-main-report. Direct competitors' revenue, willingness to pay, acquisition costs, >=50% operating automation and <=5 owner hours/week are all unverified. Recommendation: do not build the generic planner; run the paid-intent test only if it demonstrates a specific evidence or portfolio workflow customers will pay for.
